paths.description: Public entry and age-confirmation gate, representing the only complete www.dmm.co.jp surface reachable from this audit location.
Primary continuation journey: choose “I Agree”. The destination was redirected to a regional-availability denial.
Externally imposed regional-denial template reached after age confirmation; inspected as the recovery state.
Catalog, listing, product/detail, search, account, authentication and commercial flows were not covered because the service redirects this audit location to a regional block.

findings.summary: The entry surface is fixed to a light palette and does not honor the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The normal and prefers-color-scheme: dark screenshots are pixel-identical; the CSS probe found no color-scheme declaration, prefers-color-scheme rule, or light-dark() usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and define semantic surface/text colors under prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), preserving contrast in both modes.

findings.summary: The regional-denial state does not adapt to mobile and renders at a desktop scale that is extremely difficult to read.
findings.evidence: The 360x800 screenshot shows the entire denial UI compressed into a tiny cluster; DOM evidence reports no viewport meta tag and fixed pixel sizing.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a responsive viewport meta tag and use fluid/intrinsic sizing with mobile typography and spacing rather than a desktop canvas scaled down.

findings.summary: The two primary touch targets are shorter than the recommended 44 CSS pixel target size.
findings.evidence: The active-element/target probe measured both “I Agree” and “Reject” links at 240x40 CSS pixels. Keyboard focus is visible, but touch target height is only 40px.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase the interactive hit area to at least 44x44 CSS pixels while retaining the visible focus treatment.

findings.summary: A two-action gate becomes interactive much later than its content appears because of avoidable script work.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP at 0.9s but Time to Interactive at 8.4s and TBT at 210ms; the HAR attributes 1.04MB transferred to scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the gate server-rendered and defer non-essential analytics and application JavaScript until after the user acts or the browser is idle.

findings.summary: Multiple redirects and third-party script chains delay the entry document.
findings.evidence: The HAR records three consecutive first-party 302 redirects before the localized age gate; Lighthouse estimates 870ms redirect savings and reports 1,650ms document-request latency savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Route the entry URL directly to the localized gate and delay low-value third-party scripts so the critical document path remains short.

findings.summary: The minimal age gate ships a disproportionate amount of unused and duplicated analytics JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 374KiB of unused JavaScript; the HAR shows 21 script requests and 920,347 third-party bytes, including six Google Tag Manager/gtag payloads totaling about 857KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate tag containers, remove duplicate vendors, and conditionally load analytics only after consent or a user action that needs it.

findings.summary: The age gate lacks semantic page structure despite having clear visual hierarchy.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found no headings and no main, nav, header, footer, or aside landmarks; Lighthouse specifically fails landmark-one-main. Focus on the links remains visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap primary content in <main> and represent the page title/question with a logical h1/h2 hierarchy without changing the visual design.

findings.summary: The post-confirmation denial state fails mobile reflow and presents text and controls at an unusably small scale.
findings.evidence: At 360x800 the complete desktop layout is scaled into a tiny central cluster; DOM evidence confirms that the template omits meta viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and responsive type/spacing so the error and recovery controls reflow at narrow widths and zoom.

findings.summary: The entry page triggers deprecated API, DevTools Issues, and back/forward cache failures.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports one deprecated API warning, logged inspector issues, and three BFCache failure reasons.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated API usage, resolve DevTools Issues, and eliminate unload/cache-control or related blockers identified by the Lighthouse BFCache audit.

findings.summary: The site’s robots.txt is not valid according to Lighthouse.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails the robots-txt audit; the fetched robots.txt artifact is retained for correction. Entry links themselves use real href values and the age gate has a viewport meta tag.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct unsupported or malformed robots.txt directives and verify the intended public paths remain crawlable.

findings.summary: The HTTPS entry document omits baseline transport and content security headers, and several cookies are not Secure.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. The cookie audit found 3 cookies without Secure and 11 using SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS, a restrictive CSP, nosniff, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; mark all HTTPS cookies Secure and use Lax/Strict unless cross-site use is required.

findings.summary: Extensive tracking starts on the age gate before the user can enter the service or express a privacy choice.
findings.evidence: The tracker scan found 15 third-party origins and known DoubleClick, Google Tag Manager, and AppNexus trackers. HAR evidence shows 25 third-party requests and 920,347 third-party bytes on a two-link gate.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise collection on the gate, delay non-essential trackers until valid consent, and consolidate analytics into a small first-party, batched path.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent from the entry response.
findings.evidence: The header audit reports no clickjacking defense, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, CSP/frame-ancestors, or HSTS.
findings.suggestedFix: Add frame-ancestors (or X-Frame-Options as fallback), strict referrer and permissions policies, HSTS, and a nonce/hash-based CSP; evaluate Trusted Types for script-heavy surfaces.

findings.summary: The localized English gate declares Japanese as the document language.
findings.evidence: The rendered content and description are English, while the DOM probe reports <html lang="ja">. The inspected CSS also contains no logical property usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Set lang="en" on the English gate (and the correct language on every locale), provide dir where needed, and prefer logical CSS properties for translation-safe layout.

findings.summary: Background analytics work is disproportionate to the tiny gate’s user value.
findings.evidence: The HAR records 43 requests and 1,067,565 transferred bytes for a page containing two primary links; 21 requests and 1,041,721 bytes are scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove redundant tags and defer or batch any remaining measurement until consent and idle time.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts dominate the page-weight budget.
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 920,347 bytes and 25 requests; Google Tag Manager/gtag alone contributes roughly 857KB across six requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a strict third-party byte/request budget, consolidate vendors, self-host only justified dependencies, and load optional tags on demand.

findings.summary: The initial heap footprint is large for a static two-action gate.
findings.evidence: A heap summary after load contains 340,289 nodes, 1,414,953 edges, and 18,817,003 bytes of self size; this aligns with the unusually heavy analytics/script payload, though deeper retained-path analysis was not possible.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove redundant analytics and framework work from the gate, then set and monitor a heap/node budget using repeatable snapshots.

taskList.title: Minimise and consent-gate analytics, remove duplicate tag containers, and enforce a strict third-party byte/request budget.
Deploy HSTS, a restrictive nonce/hash CSP, nosniff, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and secure cookie attributes.
Repair the regional-denial template with a responsive viewport, fluid sizing, readable mobile type, and proper reflow.
Add a main landmark and logical heading hierarchy to the age gate.
Set the correct document language per localized gate and migrate layout CSS toward logical properties.
Collapse the entry redirect chain and keep non-critical scripts out of the critical document path.
Increase both decision links to at least a 44 CSS pixel hit area.
Resolve deprecated API, DevTools Issues, and BFCache blockers.
Correct invalid robots.txt directives and verify intended crawl policy.
Set and monitor a proportional heap/node budget after script reduction.
